status: LIVE design data v4: the vertical slice (milestones M1, M2a and M2b; survival_gdd.md version 4). The game and tests/survival/test_survival_data.gd read these rows. Every number is tunable.
summary: The slice's actions (M1: 13; M2a: 29 more; M2b: 4 more, 46 in all), the trap model with snares, carcass yields, world objects (the drying rack, the hung cache, staged builds) and the animation hooks they use. Every action is a technique (gated by knowledge; most are common knowledge), a recipe action (gated per recipe) or a plain verb (never gated). Fix round 1 moved casting balls and hook-and-line fishing live (redesign_balance_report.md F1-F3).
id_rules: Ids are stable strings (prefix.name). Never rename an id once saves exist; add an alias instead. Display names are separate and may change. An id is defined in exactly one place: the live file or the backlog.

milestones.M1: A winter night: fire, shelter, cold, hunger, sleep, time safety; the fort region only; one background; 1765
milestones.M2a: A winter from the woods: living from the manor woods through the winter by your own hands (gathering, hides, sewing, snares, snowshoes, a half-faced camp, a hung cache, ice fishing); plain barter with the sutler, the trader, the garrison's soldiers, a farm family from German Flatts and an old hunter; credit and the fall outfit as options; the second background
milestones.M2b: Learning from neighbours: lessons, watching, examining, quality standards, haggling, promises and loans
milestones.M3: The year turns: the full almanac, seasons and weather content, the summer goal (bark and a cabin), fishing, frogs, ginseng, one played wage job; the fur cap and robe, leggings, carving, casting balls, the cache pit, char cloth and spruce beer
milestones.M4: People: NPC schedules and tiers at the fort, standing, invitations, the soldiers and the lieutenant as mentors; Native characters only after the relevant nation's sign-off
milestones.M5: The map: the Carry, the valley, the town and the hunting grounds, travel and camps, other markets and backgrounds
milestones.post: After M5 and not yet planned: the 1757 and 1761 starts and their eras, detailed illnesses, thirst, potash, upstream canoe and bateau travel, the Proxy NPC tier, languages beyond English, French, Mohawk and Oneida

source_keys.A: Bundled animation clip names and asset IDs
source_keys.N: graph_analysis/survival/survival_gdd.md, sources list (N:3 = source N3; N33 onward added in version 3)

basis_keys.S: sourced: checked against a primary source, a scholarly work or an institutional page; web summaries and popular pages do not qualify
basis_keys.H: standard historiography (books in the GDD sources list); verify before quoting
basis_keys.H-regional: true for one region's trade or society (named in the row); not yet checked for New York
basis_keys.M: modern science or medicine sets the mechanic (period explanation may differ)
basis_keys.D: design value for balance, or a figure resting on web summaries; not a checked historical record

fields.difficulty: D for the check (skills.json check_model). 0 = no check (always succeeds).
fields.difficulty_by: alternative D by input, weather or situation
fields.time_min: game minutes of work [min, max]; the job runner picks by skill (faster when skilled)
fields.screen_s: real seconds shown on screen; the runner speeds the SimClock so time_min passes in screen_s
fields.requires: items (consumed only if also in consumes), tools (any-of lists), knowledge, near (node/world object), season window, helpers
fields.outcomes: per tier: excellent, success, partial, failure, mishap (only with a hazard)
fields.interrupt: move_cancels_keep_progress | move_cancels_lose | threat_wakes | instant | passive; any threat within 25 m interrupts a job
fields.anim: a hook id in anim_hooks below
fields.materials_at_risk: what a failure or mishap costs, shown on the prompt's second line; counts as pressure for growth
fields.technique: the action is itself a technique: its knowledge state gates it (skills.json knowledge_model); common knowledge is known by everyone
fields.plain_verb: never gated by knowledge (eating, sleeping, trading, watching)
fields.origin: the recipe book's origin note (GDD section 13, rule 9)
fields.near_all: true: every listed near tag is needed; otherwise any one
fields.give_from_stock: items taken from the node's season stock (map_regions.json resource_nodes stock)

job_runner.clock_rule: Long actions speed up the survival SimClock, never Engine.time_scale. The world keeps simulating: fires burn, animals move.

hurry.applies_to: any job with a check and a working time of 10 game minutes or more
hurry.rule: The hurry toggle trades safety for time: a third less time, a slightly worse chance, and twice the chance of a mishap (a cut on the lean-to, crushed fingers on a deadfall). It turns the cut and crushed-finger trade-offs into real choices (review 2 of v2, the trade-off issue).

world.campfire.fuel_stack: fuel items dropped within 2 m feed the fire by themselves as it burns down

quality_rules.4: the half-faced camp: three walls open to the fire

world.shelter.wind_add: chinking and banked snow add up to 1 to the shelter's wind protection (shelter.chink_bank)

world.woodpile.note: the garrison's woodpile: stacked cords count toward the firewood contract

world.drying_rack.rule: jerky hangs on the rack by the fire 1-2 game days, then is taken down; rain on an unsheltered rack slows it (the recipe's cure)

world.cache_pit.rule: Items stored in a cache do not count toward load; animals and passers-by take a little each game day (less from a hung cache of frozen meat).

world.build.rule: a staged build in progress (the half-faced camp); each stage is a resumable job of at most 120 game minutes

verbs.note: The player-facing verbs of the slice. Each verb opens the right action for what is near and carried.

M1.rule: a partial strike rolls the nurse step by itself when a flame tinder is carried
a fuel stack within 2 m feeds the fire by itself; banking is a sleep option

M2a.rule: the shot is always the player's
the trade window: goods, coin, labour; credit is optional

failure_rule.rule: On a failure about half the materials are kept or the output is downgraded; everything is lost only on a mishap, which is a listed hazard.
failure_rule.recipes: A failed craft keeps half its inputs (a single input on an even chance); a failure that still yields a product (under-dried jerky) uses all of them; a mishap loses everything.

xp_rule: base_xp 0 on plain verbs and actions with no cost and no stakes (skills.json growth_model.no_xp_actions); lessons and watching give their own points

skin_item_by_season.note: summer skins (half a buck) are backlog; in the slice every deer skin dries as a fall skin at 0.8 of its value outside October-January

carcass_yields.food_energy_note: A deer's 60 lb of venison is 6,600 game kcal: about 8 meals, 2.75 game days of eating.

trap_model.nightly_catch: lambda = F * sum over species(nightly_rate * fit * activity(month) * stock/stock0 * placement/3 * bait * set_quality); the trap holds a catch with probability (1 - exp(-lambda)); one catch per trap
trap_model.flow_rule: F is seasons.json time.flow_factor: a game night on the line stands for five calendar nights, the same factor as food and wages (review 2 of v2, the clocks issue).

placement.rule: Placement comes from what the player reads, not from the die: the site on the trail node (a run or crossing 3, a trail 2, off the trail 1), +0.5 for fresh sign of the target species found with hunt.track, minus a camp or recent gunfire nearby. The check decides build quality (set_quality), time and injury only (review 2 of v2, the placement issue).

trap_model.depletion: Per trapping cell (map_regions.json trapping_cells, 250 m squares standing for a stretch of trail country): each catch takes one animal from that cell's stock; the stock recovers 30% of its deficit each season (9 game days), a little every day. More traps in the same cells empty them faster.

unchecked.rule: A trap holds one catch. A catch left past the next morning is taken by scavengers at 35% a night; an unvisited empty trap is sprung by weather or animals at 20% a night and fishes no more until reset.

snow_reset.rule: A night of fresh snow buries or freezes a share of the sets; each needs a re-set on the next visit.

trap_model.line_limits: The line is limited by the day (checking, walking, skinning and stretching all take game minutes out of about 10-11 working hours), by the good sites in each cell, and by each cell's animals. Traps beyond what can be visited each day lose catches and stop fishing (review 2 of v2, the trap-income blocker).

season_sim.note: The data test runs a whole season (November to March) in expected values with depletion, the day's time budget, unchecked losses and snow, at 12, 24 and 48 traps for a novice and a skilled trapper, and checks the plateau. Income is cash-equivalent pence (economy.json settlement).

novice.note: Survival and Hunting about 20-30: slow, finds half the good sites, fair handling

skilled.note: Survival and Hunting about 55-65: reads every good site, tracks sign, good handling, six steel traps

trap_model.snare_note: Spring-pole snares of cordage on bent saplings take hares and rabbits for food and a fox at a low fit; snow springs them like deadfalls (K:20).

anim_notes: Clip names are the neutral aliases in source/blender_animation_index.csv; asset_id is the stable numeric id to preserve. Clips with in_frontier_library=false must be added to Frontier's Actor_B library through the godot_export pipeline, keeping native_asset_id and source_attribution metadata.
Actor_A clips need the Actor_A to Actor_B retarget planned by the melee workflow before use.
The graph-driven animation rebuild owns the AnimationTree; survival only requests a hook by id through JobRunner.

actions.name: Gather fire materials
actions.notes: The user's 'gather wood' as one verb: one interaction at deadwood gives tinder (birch or cedar bark, dry grass, punk or fungus by the node), kindling and a firewood bundle.
actions.origin: Common frontier knowledge: tinder, kindling and deadwood.

actions.name: Strike a fire (flint and steel)
actions.notes: The user's 'make fire'. A flame tinder (birch or cedar bark) in the nest adds +0.05.
actions.origin: Flint and steel: by 1765 every household on the frontier, colonial and Native, struck fire this way (GDD section 13, rule 4).

actions.name: Nurse the coal into flame
actions.notes: Runs by itself after a partial strike when a flame tinder is carried; otherwise offered as a prompt.
actions.needs_state: a smouldering coal (after a partial strike or a banked fire)
actions.origin: Common frontier knowledge.

actions.name: Add fuel

success.auto_feed: a fuel stack within 2 m of the fire feeds it by itself (world.campfire.fuel_stack)

actions.notes: No check; trivial.

actions.name: Bank the fire
actions.notes: Also a sleep-dialog option: the dialog banks the fire before sleep when fuel is stacked.

actions.origin: Common frontier knowledge: meat on a stick, cornmeal baked in the ashes.

actions.name: Take the fall outfit on the book (optional)

success.credit_line: economy.json credit (the background's first outfit, later graded by the settlement)

actions.name: Search for food plants and fibre
actions.notes: Gathers what is in season at a node in reach: nuts, acorns, grapes, Indian hemp, ramps, fiddleheads. Each node holds a season's stock (map_regions.json resource_nodes stock); a picked-out grove is empty until it refills. Yields follow the production rule (seasons.json time.production_rule).
actions.origin: Gathering nuts, greens and fibre: shared frontier knowledge; much of the plant lore came from Native neighbours; wording under consultation (GDD section 13, rule 9).

actions.name: Dig groundnuts
actions.notes: Floodplain thickets on the bottomland; half the bed's stock in the fall and half in April; not in frozen ground.
actions.origin: Groundnuts dug in fall and spring: a Native food that colonists also dug; wording under consultation (GDD section 13, rule 9).

failure.note: the pole will not bear the weight; the cordage is kept

hung.text: a meat pole lashed between two trees, any season

actions.name: Fish through the ice
actions.notes: About 6 lb in 90 minutes (0.45 meals a game hour): variety, not a replacement for the hunt. Each fish water holds a winter's stock and recovers slowly.
actions.origin: Winter fishing through the ice: Native and colonial practice alike (K:5.3).

actions.name: Build a half-faced camp (three stages)

partial.note: a gap or two to chink

failure.note: the frame came down: this stage must be done again

stage_names: the roof of boughs and bark

actions.notes: Three resumable stages of 80-120 game minutes, so no stage exceeds the 120-minute cap. Quality 4 when the last stage stands; a hatchet alone is D 27 and 1.4x the time (still capped at 120 minutes a stage). D 22 [D, tuned 2026-09 from the v4 matrix: at D 30 a Woodcraft-22 hunter needed about nine attempts and missed T4].

actions.name: Chink with moss or bank with snow
actions.origin: Common frontier knowledge: moss in the gaps, snow banked against the walls (K:4.2).

actions.name: Trade
actions.notes: The trade window (economy.json barter; SurvivalTrade): goods, coin, labour, lessons, loans and promises, both sides confirm and the authority commits. The same session serves NPCs now and players later.

actions.name: Ask to be taught
actions.notes: A lesson of 60-120 game minutes with a mentor who agrees (skills.json knowledge_model.lesson); the ask (goods, labour, friendship, a favour or a little coin, never coin only) is a trade line both confirm. Lessons give their own points; the check gives none.

actions.name: Watch someone work
actions.time: the performer's job minutes, charged to the watcher's own clock and needs
actions.notes: Within 12 m of someone at least 10 above you for 75% of the job: the work becomes seen, and 0.3 of the experience you would gain doing it (at most 1 point a day per skill; knowledge_model.watch).

actions.name: Examine how it is made
actions.notes: A finished thing in hand or in reach: the recipes that make it become heard of (never community-held knowledge).

actions.name: Haggle
actions.notes: Inside the trade window: a Trade check at D 30, +10 for each earlier press this visit. Excellent moves the ask 0.08 toward the partner's floor, success 0.05; a failure costs patience; at 0 the partner closes the window for the day. Deals under 60 d of reference value cannot be haggled (economy.json barter.haggle).

actions.name: Cast musket balls

failure.note: some of the lead spilt and must be run again

actions.notes: A Survival camp craft; Marksmanship grows only from shooting (skills.json grows_from). Live from M2a in fix round 1 (redesign_balance_report.md F1): the hunter's 3 lb of bar lead refill his pouch without a market step. Burns from hot lead (cond.injury.burn) come with that condition at M3; until then a bad cast only spills lead.
actions.materials_at_risk: half the lead on a failure
actions.origin: Casting balls from bar lead in a mould at the fire: every musket owner's camp work.

actions.name: Fish with hook and line
actions.notes: Open water only (no ice: April to November). Yields in lb of whole fish from the fish water's stock (map_regions.json node.fish_water), which the spring runs refill in April [H: verify the runs for the Mohawk's tributaries]. Live from M2a in fix round 1 (redesign_balance_report.md F1-F3): a food source that needs no powder, for the spring gap and the summer.
actions.origin: Hook-and-line fishing: common frontier practice with imported hooks; bone gorges and the fish weir are older Native technology (M3-M4).
